title: Residency Audit Bridge & Stream Reconciliation Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our existing analytics replication moves usage events across regions but lacks a non-repudiable reconciliation surface for proving per-tenant residency guarantees. Operators need a deterministic way to detect silent divergences between origin and regional materialized views, quantify exposed windows, and produce auditable proof for compliance teams and customers.

Goal: Build an audit bridge and reconciliation playbook that (1) emits compact residency assertions from the origin stream, (2) materializes lightweight checksums/watermarks in regional ingestion, (3) supports efficient divergence detection and automated repair (replay or patch apply), and (4) surfaces auditable evidence (signed assertions + repair logs) to Console and exportable compliance reports.

Scope: Streaming path (Kafka -> ingestion consumers -> ClickHouse/warehouse views), reconciliation service (stateless verifier + orchestrator), Console UI hooks for mismatches, alerting runbooks, and a migration strategy that preserves existing SLAs and throughput. This ticket covers design, prototype, and initial integration tests against staging clusters.

Out-of-scope: Full cross-region re-batching engine redesign and long-term cold-storage reconciliation (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Origin stream emits residency assertions (compact signed token) for each tenant-window partition without >5% added per-event overhead
Regional consumers persist assertions and maintain per-window checksum/watermark in a low-cardinality table
Reconciliation service detects divergence within the configured alert window (default 10m) and classifies severity
Automated repair can replay missing ranges for a tenant with an audit log entry and CI-style status flag
Console shows reconciliation status per-tenant with link to signed proof artifacts and repair timeline
E2E integration test exercising injected divergence (drop/dup events) demonstrates correct detection and repair in staging
steps: Design assertion format: include tenant_id, window_start, window_end, event_count, rolling checksum, signer_id, signature
Add lightweight signer at origin ingestion (signing via service KMS key) and emit assertion messages to assertions topic
Modify regional consumers to persist assertion records and compute local window checksum for cross-check
Implement reconciliation service: pulls assertion stream, compares to persisted regional checksums, emits mismatch records and repair actions
Provide repair adapters: (a) range replay orchestrator that replays from origin topic, (b) patch applier for denormalized materialized views
Console integration: API endpoints for proof retrieval, per-tenant reconciliation tab, severity alerts and manual repair trigger
Create chaos test harness to inject omission/duplication and measure detection latency and repair success
Run compliance review and produce exportable proof bundles (signed assertions + repair log) for legal/Customer Success
risks: Signing adds CPU/KMS latency at origin under peak QPS — mitigable via batching and ephemeral signing tokens
Assertion topic could become high-cardinality if windows are too fine-grained — mitigate via tenant bucketing and adaptive windows
Automated repair could lead to duplicate-side effects in downstream sinks if idempotency not enforced — requires idempotent replay adapters
Cross-region clock skew can cause window misalignment; reconciliation must support time-skew tolerant matching
Large-scale repairs may stress network egress and Dedicated capacity — include rate limits and repair budgets per-tenant
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff doc posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANAL/Residency+Audit+Bridge (prototype format and benchmark plan).

2026-02-18 - Lucas Moretti: Implemented origin assertion prototype (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/284). Benchmarked signing overhead: ~0.9% CPU at 80th percentile when batching assertions per 1s window.
2026-02-25 - Keisha Wong (SRE): Raised concern about assertion topic retention and GC costs; suggested compacted topic + TTL on proof store. Added to design trade-offs.
2026-03-02 - PM review (Rafael Diaz): Requested acceptance criteria explicitly include Console exportable proof bundles for legal. Added to ACs.

2026-03-07 - Engineering: Reconciliation service skeleton implemented; initial mismatch classification logic (missing-range vs checksum-mismatch) checked in (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/19).

2026-03-10 - Security (Lena O'Connor): Reviewed signing approach. Recommended using per-environment signing keys in KMS with rotation and inclusion of signer_id in assertion. Security review required: true.
notes_for_rollout: Start rollout in staged geo (us-west-2 origin, eu-west-1 regional). Enable assertions in dry-run mode for 48h, monitor Console reconciliation dashboard, then enable active repair for opt-in tenants only. Provide a 'repair budget' default of 10GB/day per-tenant to avoid noisy repairs. Communicate to beta customers via release notes and scheduled maintenance window.
implementation_notes: Prefer compact binary assertion (protobuf) for network efficiency. Use SHA-256 rolling window checksum seeded by tenant salt. Persist assertions in a small key-value store (region-local ClickHouse table or DynamoDB) optimized for low-latency lookups. Design reconciliation service to be horizontally scalable and eventually-consistent; use leader election per-tenant-window to avoid duplicate repair triggers.
next_steps: Complete sign/verify integration with KMS (blocking: security cert rotation policy)
Wire regional consumer assertion persistence and local checksum compute
Add reconciliation alerts to PagerDuty runbook and Console incidents view
Schedule staged rollout and run chaos injection tests
